questions.prompt: Which protocol is used to transfer web pages from a server to a browser?
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — HTTP (or its secure form HTTPS) transfers hypertext web pages.
questions.feedbackWrong: HTTP is the web protocol. FTP transfers files, SMTP sends email, POP3 retrieves email.

mistakes.misconception: Confuses file transfer with web page transfer.
mistakes.correction: FTP is for bulk file transfer between systems; browsers use HTTP(S) to fetch pages and their resources.

mistakes.misconception: Mixes up email protocols with web protocols.
mistakes.correction: SMTP pushes mail between servers — it never delivers web content.

questions.prompt: In the TCP/IP model, which layer is responsible for routing packets across networks?
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — the Internet layer (IP) handles logical addressing and routing.
questions.feedbackWrong: Routing by IP address happens at the Internet layer. Transport handles end-to-end segments; Link handles the physical hop.

mistakes.misconception: Confuses TCP's end-to-end delivery with IP's routing.
mistakes.correction: TCP (transport) gives reliable ordered delivery between endpoints; ROUTING decisions are IP's job at the internet layer.

questions.prompt: Compare circuit switching and packet switching, giving one advantage of each.
questions.guidance: Think about how the path is used during communication.

markScheme.text: Circuit switching establishes a dedicated path for the whole conversation; packet switching splits data into packets routed independently.
Packets may take different routes and are reassembled at the destination using sequence numbers.
Circuit switching advantage: guaranteed bandwidth / consistent latency once established — suits real-time voice.
Packet switching advantage: efficient shared use of links / fault tolerance — packets reroute around failures.

mistakes.misconception: Assumes packet switching is uniformly superior in speed.
mistakes.correction: Packet switching shares bandwidth efficiently but individual packets can be delayed or lost; circuit switching guarantees constant rate once set up.

questions.prompt: A file of 50 megabytes is transmitted over a connection of 20 megabits per second. Calculate the transfer time in seconds (assume 1 megabyte = 8 megabits).
What is the key difference between symmetric and asymmetric encryption?
options: Symmetric uses one shared key; asymmetric uses a public-private key pair
Symmetric is always stronger than asymmetric
Asymmetric encryption cannot be used on the internet
Symmetric encryption requires no keys at all
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — symmetric: same key encrypts and decrypts; asymmetric: public key encrypts, private key decrypts.
questions.feedbackWrong: Symmetric encryption uses ONE shared key both ways. Asymmetric uses a mathematically linked pair — public to encrypt, private to decrypt.

mistakes.correction: Strength depends on key length and algorithm, not the symmetric/asymmetric distinction — asymmetric's advantage is key distribution, not raw strength.

questions.prompt: Describe how a man-in-the-middle attack works on an unencrypted network connection, and name one countermeasure.

markScheme.text: Attacker positions themselves between the two communicating parties, intercepting traffic.
They can read, alter or relay messages while both parties believe they communicate directly.
Countermeasure: encryption with authentication — TLS/HTTPS with certificates verifies the endpoint identity.

questions.prompt: A school chooses a star topology for its LAN. Describe the structure and give one advantage and one disadvantage.

markScheme.text: Every device connects individually to a central switch/hub — no direct device-to-device links.
Advantage: failure of one cable/device doesn't affect the rest; easy to add devices; central management.
Disadvantage: the central switch is a single point of failure; more cable required than a bus.

questions.prompt: A network has the subnet mask 255.255.255.0. How many host addresses does this allow per subnet (including network and broadcast addresses)?
State two differences between client-server and peer-to-peer networks.

markScheme.text: Client-server has dedicated central servers providing services; peer-to-peer shares resources directly between equal peers.
Client-server centralises security/backups but costs more and has a server single point of failure; P2P is cheap and resilient but harder to secure and manage.
